claim.date_text_original: Tōdai-specific 奴婢 records in 751/756 and a 792 emancipation petition
claim.summary: Tōdai-ji has target-specific eighth-century evidence for legally non-free 奴/奴婢 status. Tōdai slave-register documents are attested in the mid-eighth century, and a 792 Nihon Kōki entry records Tōdai administrators successfully petitioning to release named temple 奴 into 良 status. Specialist scholarship treats Tōdai 奴婢 organization and service as a substantive historical institution. The atlas therefore records a bounded positive slavery/servile-slave status claim for the documented institutional horizon, without treating all temple construction, corvée, estate labour or later shōen dependency as slavery.
claim.notes: Consolidates accepted EXP-13 / post-D099 internal review into claim-centric research state. The research target was 800 CE, but this claim interval stops at the last decisive documented event (792) rather than fabricating an exact-800 roster or persistence claim.

territorial_practice.notes: Positive legally non-free 奴/奴婢 status at Tōdai-ji. No prevalence, workforce share, all-labour classification or estate-wide practice extent is inferred.
